newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Roh, Chun arrive in Seoul court for appeals verdict.
newsitem.headline: Roh, Chun arrive in Seoul court for appeals verdict.

text.p: Former South Korean presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo arrived at a Seoul court on Monday to hear the verdict of their appeals against conviction for treason, mutiny and bribery.
Chun was sentenced to death and Roh to 22-1/2 years in jail at their trial in August. They are appealing along with 25 former aides and business tycoons convicted with them.
The two former heads of state arrived separately in blue prison busses in a convoy of police jeeps with flashing lights and television cars.

Judges first deliver the verdict on the mutiny and treason convictions over a 1979 coup masterminded by Chun and a massacre of pro-democracy demonstrators the following year in the southwest city of Kwangju.
They will then pass judgement on the bribery convictions.
The "trial of the century" could drag on for months longer if the case reaches the Supreme Court.
